subject: Post-call: WiredB streaming concurrency & temporary rate increase
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@wiredb.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap — concurrency, streaming, and temporary quota request

Sam — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary of what we heard from WiredB:
- Latency SLO: 95th pct <= 300ms for single-turn generation (avg seq len ~150 tokens).
- Streaming: client needs server-sent events for partial tokens, target first-byte <120ms and steady streaming at ~15 tokens/sec.
- Concurrency: production peak ~850 parallel user requests, typical fanout per session 1.5 calls/sec.
- Connection pooling: you will multiplex many logical sessions over fewer TCP connections from edge devices (HTTP/2).
- Bursting: higher load expected for batch ETL windows (~3x baseline for 10min).

Redwood constraints / asks from our side:
- Default hosted rate limits would throttle at 400 parallel request slots for your account. We can allow temporary elevated concurrency for the POC while we validate latency under load.
- For streaming, we recommend using HTTP/2 or WebSocket with keepalive and smaller chunk sizes (64–128 tokens) to reduce head-of-line blocking.
- Connection pool guidance: aim for 16–24 logical sessions per persistent connection to avoid excessive TLS handshakes while keeping HTTP/2 streams manageable.

Proposed action items (mutual action plan):
1) Redwood will provision a temporary concurrency bump to 900 parallel slots for a 2-week POC window (subject to traffic shaping). Action: Marissa to approve provisioning.
2) WiredB to run the provided connection matrix in the attachment (WiredB-conn-matrix.xlsx) and return actual device multiplexing ratios and average seq lengths by Dec 3.
3) Redwood infra (Ben/Engineering) will run a targeted load test with streaming enabled on Dec 5–6 and share a latency profile report.
4) Draft SLA reflecting the elevated POC quota and rollback triggers is attached (SLA-draft-WiredB.pdf). Procurement to confirm by Dec 10.

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Do you need guaranteed ordering for streamed chunks, or can the client assemble out-of-order chunks?
- Will you use a single model variant in the POC, or do you plan automatic fallback to a smaller model on overload?

Please reply with any edits to the MAP and confirm procurement contact for the SLA. If this summary looks good, Marissa will initiate the temporary quota change.

Thanks — Priyom
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: WiredB-conn-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 32KB)
Attachment: SLA-draft-WiredB.pdf (PDF, 85KB)

From: Sam Patel <sam@wiredb.com>

Cc: procurement@wiredb.com
Date: 2026-11-30T18:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — concurrency, streaming, and temporary quota request

Thanks, Priyom — that captures the conversation. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Ordering: we require strict ordering for partial responses when the client is doing token-by-token UI updates. Out-of-order assembly would add complexity to the client.
2) Fallback model: for the POC we want a smaller fallback model to keep latency predictable; auto-fallback is acceptable if Redwood can keep tokenization and response formatting consistent.
3) Connection multiplexing: most devices will hold 2 persistent connections; aggregation happens in a regional gateway (approx 1:8 multiplex ratio). We’ll fill out the attached matrix by EOD Dec 3.

Also — is the temporary concurrency bump billed at standard hosted rates or do you have a POC pricing credit? Procurement is looped here to understand cost.

Sam
CTO, WiredB

Sam — quick answers inline to make procurement/scheduling easier.

Ordering: understood — we will keep strict ordering for streamed chunks during the POC. Engineering notes: we’ll enable sequence IDs on each chunk and keep a small reorder buffer server-side to handle transient reordering inside our infra, ensuring the client receives ordered SSE events.

Fallback model: Redwood can configure auto-fallback to a pinned smaller variant (same tokenizer) so formatting is stable. We’ll include model fingerprints in eval logs so you can correlate regressions.

Temporary quota billing: Marissa — can you confirm POC billing treatment? My recommendation: extend a 30% hosted credit for the 2-week elevated quota, then revert to standard usage billing.

Ben/Engineering (cc): we’ll need a validated load test plan that exercises 15–20 tokens/sec streaming at 900 parallel slots with the 3x burst window. Ben, can you confirm the test harness and preferred date?

Next steps (updated):
- WiredB: fill conn matrix by 12/03 (Sam) — status: in progress.
- Redwood infra: run load test 12/05–12/06, share raw metrics and percentile latency curves.
- Redwood sales: provision 900 slot temporary concurrency window for 2 weeks once Procurement signs the button on the SLA.

If procurement prefers, we can stage the quota increase in two increments (600 then 900) to reduce risk.

Thanks — Priyom

1) Quota & billing: We can provide a 2-week elevated concurrency window to 900 parallel slots at hosted rates with a 30% POC credit applied to usage for the window. After the window ends we’ll continue at standard per-token/embedding rates unless you sign a reserved Dedicated commitment.

2) SLA and procurement: I’ve attached an editable SLA (SLA-draft-WiredB.pdf) and a DocuSign link for approvals. If legal needs redlines we’ll run them through our contracts team; turnaround typically 3–5 business days for minor edits.

3) Operational: we’ll schedule the load test for Dec 5 (engineers prefer PST morning window). Priyom / Ben will send the test plan Monday morning.

Please confirm: (a) acceptance of the 2-week 900-slot POC window with 30% credit, and (b) whether you want staged ramp (600 -> 900). Once you confirm I’ll request infra to provision and send the DocuSign link.

Best — Marissa
